title: Metropolitan Museum of Art cancels John Galliano exhibition after weeks of backlash
dek: The Metropolitan Museum of Art cancelled a planned 2027 exhibition of fashion designer John Galliano's work after weeks of public backlash over his 2011 antisemitic remarks conviction. Galliano himself announced the decision on Monday, stating the exhibition would not take place 'at this time,' citing his commitment to ongoing atonement.
author: The GoCheckMyNews Desk
key_fact: The Met cancelled a planned 2027 Galliano exhibition after donors threatened to rescind gifts, Jewish community leaders and city officials objected, and the designer himself withdrew from the honour, citing the pain caused by his past remarks.
bottom_line: The cancelled exhibition leaves open the question of whether and when a major cultural institution might reconsider honouring a designer whose 2011 conviction for antisemitic conduct continues to provoke community opposition, particularly as the museum prepares an alternative exhibition for spring 2027.
body:
The Metropolitan Museum of Art cancelled a planned exhibition of John Galliano's work set to open in May 2027 after weeks of backlash over his 2011 conviction for antisemitic remarks. Galliano announced the decision Monday in a statement to the museum.
"After much reflection and discussion with the Met and all those involved, I have decided, with great sadness, that it is best for the exhibition not to take place at this time," Galliano stated, per BBC reporting. The exhibition, titled "John Galliano: Horizons," was due to coincide with the 2027 Met Gala on May 3, which fell on Yom HaShoah (Holocaust and Heroism Remembrance Day).
In his statement, Galliano acknowledged his past conduct and said, "I remain fully accountable for the pain caused by my words in the past, particularly the hurt I caused to the Jewish and Asian communities, and I remain deeply sorry for it." He noted his "15 years of sobriety and recovery from alcoholism and addiction" and stated, "I understand that meaningful atonement is not achieved through an exhibition, institutional recognition or a single public gesture. It is a continuing responsibility, demonstrated through listening, learning and one's conduct over time."
Galliano served as creative director of Dior for 15 years before his dismissal in 2011, according to CBS News reporting. He was found guilty of abusing a Jewish curator in a Paris restaurant, per BBC. A court heard that in separate incidents, Galliano hurled racist insults at the curator's friend, who is of South Asian origin, and declared a love for Hitler. His lawyer at the time blamed the behaviour on "work-related stress and multiple addictions."
Galliano became creative director of Maison Margiela in 2014, a post he held until 2024. BBC reported that Galliano was set to become only the third living designer to be the subject of a solo show at the Met's Costume Institute, per CBS News.
In recent weeks, donors threatened to rescind gifts to the museum if the exhibition moved forward as planned, according to CBS News reporting. Julie Menin, speaker of New York City Council, said, per BBC, "After my numerous and lengthy meetings and conversations with the Met, I am pleased that they have agreed to not honour John Galliano. From the beginning, I have told them that I strongly disagreed with this decision, and at this rising time of antisemitism, it had served as a gut punch to the Jewish community. This is the correct decision, as the harm and pain this was causing was simply unacceptable."
Jonathan Greenblatt, chief executive of the Anti-Defamation League, said that with antisemitism at "crisis levels," honouring Galliano would be "misguided," per BBC reporting. "Even Galliano ultimately recognised what the Met should have done from the start. This was the wrong move at the wrong moment. Timing matters," Greenblatt said.
Andrew Bolton, curator in charge of the Met's Costume Institute, stated, according to CBS News, "I believe deeply in the responsibility of museums to examine difficult histories with rigor, candor, and care. I also recognize the pain and concern this exhibition has caused."
The Met confirmed in a statement that the "Spring 2027 exhibition devoted to his four-decade oeuvre will not proceed as planned" and said it will announce details on a new spring Costume Institute exhibition and the 2027 Met Gala at a later date, per CBS News.
